site.title: AthenIQ Workforce
site.tagline: Applied AI training for Massachusetts employers
site.description: AthenIQ Workforce is the workforce development division of AthenIQ Institute. Its first program delivers Focused AI Skills Training (FAST AI) to Massachusetts employers and their workers.

programs.name: Focused AI Skills Training (FAST AI)
programs.audience: Massachusetts employers and the incumbent or newly hired workers they enroll
programs.summary: Instructor-led, applied AI training for the tools and tasks a worker already does. Six stackable courses take an employee from how a model behaves to prompting, analysis, occupation-specific workflows, management and governance — each course a set of live multi-agent classrooms with exercises built from the employer's own work.

funding.administrator: Commonwealth Corporation, a quasi-public arm of the Massachusetts Executive Office of Labor and Workforce Development, with the Executive Office of Economic Development
funding.cost: No cost to an eligible employer. Commonwealth Corporation purchases training slots from approved providers and reimburses completed enrollments, so the employer pays no tuition for approved courses.
terms: Course costs may not exceed $300 per instructional hour per training slot, or $3,000 per person per course, whichever is less.
A provider's total award may not exceed $400,000, covering all of its approved courses.
Contracts run for up to two years; match contributions are not required.
Enrollment, attendance and completion are tracked and reported to Commonwealth Corporation by the provider.

timeline: Provider RFQ applications were due November 6, 2026, with award decisions expected in mid-December 2026.
The program opens for employer enrollment in January 2027.
Training is prioritised where it starts on or after February 1, 2027 and finishes by June 30, 2028.
delivery: Instructor-led: every chapter runs as a live multi-agent classroom — an AI teacher, AI classmates, and the learner doing the work.
Applied: each exercise uses an artifact from the worker's own role, tools and day-to-day tasks rather than generic AI literacy content.
Tracked: attendance, completion and assessment are recorded in the LMS and reported to the program.
Stackable: the six courses can be taken as a certificate ladder or individually against an employer's training plan.
outcomes: Explain what a language model does, where it fails, and how to verify an AI draft before it is used.
Write prompts and build repeatable AI workflows for the work the learner already owns.
Analyse data and produce reports with AI assistance, checking the result against the source.
Apply AI to the tasks of a specific occupation, with that occupation's own examples and constraints.
Lead AI adoption: choose use cases, set review steps, and measure whether the work improved.
Govern AI use: data handling, disclosure, bias and risk review under an organisation's policy.

courseDescriptions.FAI101: What a language model actually does, which tasks to hand it, what data may go in, and the verification habit every AI draft needs before it is used.
courseDescriptions.FAI102: Briefs instead of wishes: prompts that state the task, the source and the standard, iteration that converges, and a prompt library a team can share.
courseDescriptions.FAI103: From a business question to a checked answer: what AI analysis can and cannot tell you, assisted analysis with checks, and reporting for a decision.
courseDescriptions.FAI104: Map the work before automating it, build the workflow on the tools the role already uses, handle client-facing work, then pilot, measure and hand it over.
courseDescriptions.FAI105: A manager's map of AI, process improvement rather than tool envy, what changes for roles and people, and the business case with its rules attached.
courseDescriptions.FAI106: The frameworks that apply, a risk assessment you can defend, transparency and worker rights, and vendor review with an incident response path.
